correctness.rationale: On e1=e2=e3 the Jacobian rows are 1,-xi,xi²; any rank drop imposes at most two coordinate values, excluded by m=1 and m=2 explicit substitution. A complete-intersection connectedness theorem and adjunction give smooth geometrically integral genus four. The three-cycle is fixed-point-free in characteristic three, hence its quotient is finite étale. Symmetric-polynomial elimination yields a cubic with discriminant D, and the Vandermonde generates the fixed quadratic subfield of the degree-six map. Coprimality of D(T,1) and T³-T proves the quotient is a smooth genus-two curve. The exact identity z=(a-b)/(u+v), σz=z+1 and W=(u+v)³(z³-z) gives a nontrivial Artin–Schreier extension and trivial ramification by freeness. Exact SymPy verifier reproduced the discriminant, identity, all rank-drop cases, base-point exclusion, squarefreeness and Cartier-Manin identity. Ordinary genus-two quotient gives p-rank four by Deuring–Shafarevich. Mathematical proof covers all geometric points, not merely sampled finite fields.

value.rationale: The integral elementary-symmetric reduction is forced by the classical quintic-root geometry but differs dramatically from the naive power-sum reduction at the bad prime three. The precise connected, everywhere-unramified Artin–Schreier class W/(u+v)^3 specifies a nontrivial class in H¹_et of a natural ordinary genus-two curve, representing arithmetic torsor information neither recovered from the known complex quotient genus nor from the known Q-isogeny class. Its explicit form makes the wild quotient usable for finite-characteristic Jacobian and geometric descent questions. No claim of first genus-two quotient or standalone first p-rank computation is made.
